_comment: G9: near-band client rules over plain.jtl, built from Java's exact stats. Every number the CI/CD
JSON and the JUnit XML write beside a band must stay on its own side of every band the rule
declares, warn and fail alike: a FAIL is never written on the band it breached, a PASS never on
or across its fail band. No other golden sits within 24 of a band, so none of them can see it.
Each threshold is pinned to plain.jtl's measured value (the mean of GET /api/products 119.4675, of
POST /api/checkout 373.8625, the overall mean 234.9117..., throughput 8.2989...) and is not
realistic. Percentiles are whole milliseconds since 4.2.6 (exact counts, B2), so no percentile can
sit within a hundredth of a band; the per-sampler rules that used p50/p75 read the sampler's mean.
realistic. Q12's never-zero, float noise (L8) and the 1e9 cases cannot be built from this JTL;
CiCdJsonSerializerTest, JunitXmlWriterTest and digits-vectors.json pin those.
